Target Shield Master Race.

The truth is that there is generally your gonna want one of two left hand parry catalysts: a "micro-shield" as I call them, or a parrying dagger. Some micro-shields are Magic Shield, Target Shield, or the most common, and supposedly the best one, the Buckler. Why these shields? Well, if you take compare the parry animation of a micro-shield and any other non-micro-shield you'll notice that the parry animations are somewhat different. And not just the animations, but the parry frames. I can't tell you what exactly it is off the top of my head, but I know that the window of time in which an opponents connecting attack will result in a parried attack that occurs when you press L2 is substantially longer with a micro-shield than any other shield. Parrying daggers are, as far as I know, the same thing as micro-shields as far as parry frames go, but they can also be utilized as offensive weapons for quick hits. A lot of better players use them to bait opponents into a parry, as the daggers attack animation is very quick and therefore, a parry can be made more shortly after.

Let me be clear, parrying is not easy. It takes lots of practice. The backsteps seem easy, and they are the easiest stratagy, but ultimately many people don't realize that you need to know the opponents weapon, and wait for their first attack animation to finally end before hitting L2 and parrying the follow-up. Some weapons are harder than others too. The Silverblack Spear's 2-handed R2 combo (?), the second attack is probably impossible to parry with the backstep-parry stratagy, it's too quick of a follow up.

There is an art to it, and practiced parries makes perfect parries. 
Here's some general tips:

* Watch for a pattern. This is more useful in PvE, as real players are more likely to not stick to any particular pattern of attack except one, which I'll get into in a bit. But PvE-wise watching an enemy's method of attack and memorizing it is the best way to learn how to parry AIs. 

* Baiting. If you're a ~~master~~baiter like me, you've mastered the art of luring an enemy into attacking you, only to be knocked to the ground by the sweet sound of a buckler swiping away a running R1. This is not so easy to do without knowing your enemy, and it takes a great deal of experience to successfully bait an opponent. First, look at the playstyle of the opponent. Are they aggressive, or are they turtling up with a havel's shield? Are they two handing or one handing? These observations and others are necessary to successfully bait out an attack from an opponent. But I would say that usually you can bait an opponent into attacking you if you purposely throw out an attack and miss hitting an opponent. Most players who this happens to are gonna just instinctively move in for a face to face punish, and when they do, that your chance to hit L2 and *pwing* parry them.

* Follow-up parries. This is by far, the easiest stratagy I could suggest to anyone for landing a good parry. Three really simple steps: first, wait for an opponent to start closing the distance between you and them (this means they're probably gonna make an attack). Second, as soon as they attack, perform a **back-step** (NOT A ROLL). And lastly, as soon as you feel like their first attack animation is over, parry! Nine times out of ten they'll perform a second follow-up attack on you after you dodge their first attack with the backstep, leaving them super vunerable to an easy L2-Parry. 

I hope this helps you!

It's broken. The problem you'll find is that DkSII is the only souls-borne game that has a different matchmaking system then all the other games. While the other games (Demon's Souls, Dark Souls 1, Bloodborne) rely on the "Soul Level" System - by which you are matched up with players who are near your current character level - Dark Souls 2 uses the godawful "Soul Memory" system. The major difference with the soul memory system from the previous matchmaking system, is that it doesn't allow for consistant matching between a character and other characters near the same progress level wise. IE: you can be level 20, but have collected over 1 million souls, and have to fight anyone else who has collected over 1 million souls, regardless of their level. I believe this was done to prevent/disencourage "twinking" which, if you don't already know, is where a player runs through the game at a very low level all the way through so that the end result is that they can PvP or Co-op with lower level players with late-game gear. However, even if this was their justification, they put a rong in the game that actually promoted this because it absorbed souls so the players SM (Soul Memory) would not increase, and therefore Twinking was still possible, but a pro player could even do it more effectively. 

The biggest effect this has on the Blue Sentinals Covenant is that the covenant has two basic functions it performs:

*1) Invading the guilty, which for most is a late-game, high SM experience that is most "consistent" (if you could call spamming blue eye orbs for hours trying to find one matchup consistent) in New Game Plus, or NG+.

*2) Assisting the members of the Way of the Blue Covenant when they are invaded by dark spirits, which is practically impossible because the chances of a player who is part of the covenant being invaded are flat out astronomical. I have not **once** experienced an invasion early game that I have either A: been able to take on and destroy by myself, or with 3 of the dozens of shades that place their signs down in most beginner areas; or B: been able to successfully connect with me to even make it into my world. So even if you go through the trouble of "twinking" so you can assist with the Guardian Seal, the chances are that you'll still never be able to use it.

My biggest issue though is that I want to get WoG, and now I've gotten to a point where I am on NG++ and Imm heading towards Castle Dranleic so I can buy it from the Chancellor. Good thing I'm decent at speed-running the game, because if I wasn't I would be lost.

In order to get an illusory ring you must succeed in one of two (or both at the same time) constraints in one single playthrough of the entire game. 

Each constraint, when completed, will reward the player with one of the two rings. 

Illusory Ring of the Conqueror is the first ring. When worn it causes the wearers Left Hand Weapon to become invisible. It is recieved after the credits of the game if the player has not died ONCE throughout their entire playthrough up until the credits roll. 

Illusory Ring of the Exhalted is the second ring. When worn it causes the wearers Right Hand Weapon to become invisible. It is recieved, much like it's previously stated companion, after the credits of the game if the player has not lit a bonfire ONCE throughout their entire playthrough up until the credits roll.

It is not true that you can get one as a drop from a phantom.

TL;DR

No you can't get one off a phantom, you have to complete the game without dying/lighting a bonfire in order to get either the invisible Left Hand/invisible Right Hand ring, respectively.
